08-1.title: What a framework gives you
08-1.tldr: Raw API = request → response. A framework adds the surrounding machinery: session/state, context management, a tool registry, a control loop, streaming, tracing, and guardrails.

08-2.title: Graph vs role frameworks
08-2.tldr: Graph-based makes control flow an explicit graph of nodes/edges over shared state (deterministic, inspectable); role-based makes the unit an agent with a role that collaborates (flexible, less deterministic).
points: Role: agents with roles that collaborate.

08-3.title: Choosing a framework
08-3.tldr: Pick by control shape and state model: explicit graph/routing with durable state → LangGraph; role/team collaboration for fast multi-agent → CrewAI; a managed agent SDK for host-managed agents.
points: Managed agent SDK for hosted agents.
Match the framework to the control shape.

08-4.title: Heavier framework vs custom
08-4.tldr: Heavy frameworks give batteries (tools, memory, permissions, teams, observability) at the cost of startup time, learning curve, config surface, and churn; light custom code is transparent but you build the plumbing.
points: Choose by team size, rate of change, control needs.

08-5.title: Unnecessary abstraction
08-5.tldr: The framework adds abstraction when the app is a single model call, when its node/agent/state model forces you to reshape logic, or when the graph is actually a straight line — warning signs include fighting the framework.
points: Single model call doesn't need a framework.
Forcing business logic into nodes/agents is a smell.
A straight line disguised as a graph.

08-6.title: When abstractions don't fit
08-6.tldr: Use escape hatches: implement the base interface directly, call the primitive without the wrapper, override hooks, or replace a component; if there's no seam, that's a real limitation.
points: Call the primitive (model/tool) without the wrapper.
Override hooks or replace a component.

08-7.title: Which node runs next
08-7.tldr: A scheduler activates every node whose input channels are ready, runs them (often concurrently), routes outputs to successors, and repeats until no node is active.

08-8.title: Versioning & rolling back workflows
08-8.tldr: Treat the agent/workflow definition as a versioned artifact: immutable versions with a content hash, activate one, list history, roll back atomically — prompts are only a subset.
points: Version the whole definition, not just prompts.

08-9.title: Will a framework scale with your team
08-9.tldr: Look for declarative registration and plugins, stable extension contracts, provider/config abstraction, schema'd config, and real docs. Be wary if every change means patching internals.
